criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies Voss DLA Section 4.3 sublicensing restriction conflict
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 2 identifies DLA 4.3(b) bar on Derivative Access to Derivative Models for any third party with >25 Hospital Facilities absent Voss prior written consent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Notes Kaelen's 43 hospitals exceed Voss DLA 25-facility threshold
criteria_results.reasoning: Explicitly states Kaelen operates 43 hospitals, well above the 25-facility threshold.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Recommends obtaining Voss consent or other mitigation
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends submitting Voss consent request by May 2, 2025 and making Voss consent a condition precedent; also alternate data sources.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies DLA breach/termination risk to Atherton's data supply
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes pilot/deployment without consent risks breach of 4.3(b), Voss audit, 60-day cure/termination right, and loss of the data feed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies Voss DLA expiration vs. Kaelen license term mismatch
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies DLA expiry 12/31/2027 (max 12/31/2030 on renewal) versus Kaelen term to 6/30/2032 (up to 2038), showing the gap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Notes impact on model update obligations and training capability
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains Atherton could not retrain/update with Voss data post-expiry while bound to quarterly updates and performance obligations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003a: Identifies Section 7.4 investor consent requirement for exclusive licenses exceeding 3 years or covering >30% of a market segment
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies IRA 7.4 prior written consent of Lead Investor Director Samir Okafor for exclusive licenses >3 years or >30% of a Defined Market Segment.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003b: Identifies that the proposed 7-year Kaelen license triggers the Ridgeline consent requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: States trigger (i) is clearly met by the 7-year Initial Term.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Notes consent has not been formally obtained
criteria_results.reasoning: States consent is not in hand, informal briefing does not satisfy 7.4, and describes material breach of IRA and injunctive/specific performance remedies.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004a: Identifies HIPAA de-identification standard is unspecified in term sheet
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 11 notes 'De-identified' and 'in accordance with applicable law' are undefined for the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide data license.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004b: References HIPAA de-identification methods (Safe Harbor or Expert Determination)
criteria_results.reasoning: References Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods under 45 C.F.R. 164.514(b).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Flags 'irrevocable' data license as problematic
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo treats the irrevocable data license as a valuable asset to protect and does not flag irrevocability as problematic if de-identification proves inadequate.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies antitrust/competition concerns with 30-mile exclusivity radius
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 25 flags antitrust sensitivity of up-to-13-year territorial restraint around 43 facilities, rule-of-reason scrutiny and private claims.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Notes overlapping radii could block entire metropolitan areas
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 8 notes 43 overlapping 30-mile circles across nine states would cover many major metropolitan markets including Atherton's home market.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies conflict with Pinnacle 'no impairment' clause
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies Pinnacle 9.2 no-impairment covenant (with cure/termination/refund remedy) and update-parity risk from Kaelen-specific terms and possible Voss impairment as issues the deal must respect.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Recommends mitigation for Pinnacle conflict
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends update parity across licensees, grandfathering existing licensees, and ensuring Kaelen terms don't restrict updates to others.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies undefined concordance methodology in Performance Threshold
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies Kaelen selects the validation dataset, Kaelen radiologists as ground truth, and undefined protocol (case mix, stratification, exclusions).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Notes this creates unilateral termination risk for Kaelen
criteria_results.reasoning: States the threshold is effectively a Kaelen option to exit since Kaelen controls the inputs and benefits from failure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies perpetual royalty-free improvement license surviving termination
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 5 identifies the perpetual, royalty-free license to Improvements surviving termination, letting Kaelen use the platform free forever.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies compound risk with source code escrow provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: Connects penalty-free performance termination with retention of the perpetual Improvements license (Issues 5 and 9) and escrow release via breach triggers.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies SOC 2 Type II certification gap
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies Type I only (Greystone, Aug 10, 2024), Type II requires an observation period and is expected Q3 2025, creating Day-1 breach at July 1, 2025.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Recommends grace period or condition precedent for SOC 2 Type II
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends grace period with Type I plus bridge letter, phased compliance, CP fallback, and remedy carve-outs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies FDA 510(k) clearance scope vs. deployment model tension
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies K223847 clears a CADe assistive tool not for autonomous diagnosis; 'primary diagnostic screening' risks new 510(k)/De Novo and termination trigger.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies source code escrow overbreadth — model weights and training pipelines
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies escrow includes model weights and training pipelines, Atherton's highest-tier trade secrets, enabling Kaelen to retrain and replicate ClearSight AI.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Notes escrow release of model weights may violate Voss DLA
criteria_results.reasoning: States depositing/releasing weights (a Derivative Model) to Kaelen conflicts with DLA 4.3(a)-(b) and needs Voss consent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies MFL clause metric mismatch (per-image vs. flat fees)
criteria_results.reasoning: MFL analysis notes per-image fees are undefined but does not identify that licensees pay flat annual fees making the per-image comparison a metric mismatch.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies retroactive adjustment / cash-flow risk
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies retroactive repricing creating refund liability exceeding the liability cap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013: Identifies cumulative update rejection and platform divergence risk
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 15 notes unlimited update rejection with indefinite support of whatever version is in production, causing version fragmentation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013: Notes downstream impacts of divergence (support, improvements, performance)
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies burden of supporting legacy versions, cost and regulatory/cybersecurity risk.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014: Identifies payment terms / cash-flow mismatch with deployment timeline
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes Year 1 front-loaded deployment costs for 43 sites paid quarterly in arrears net-60, first payment ~5 months after Effective Date.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014: Recommends milestone payments or accelerated payment terms
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends non-refundable deployment fee at signing/milestones and fees in advance, net-30.
